subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discussion with Caduceus Health / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sramirez@caduceus.health>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discussion with Caduceus Health / next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks again for your time today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can surface the next steps to procurement.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Current on-prem inference has intermittent latency spikes during batch processing and nightly SLAs are frequently missed.
- Data isolation/regulatory requirement: PHI-handling pipelines must be isolated from other tenants and auditable.
- Predictable unit economics needed for budgeting (prefer committed monthly spend).

Goals you mentioned:
- Move to a reserved GPU pool for inference to eliminate cold-starts and control latency (target p95 < 120ms for 512-token model paths).
- Strict isolation for PHI workloads (dedicated tenancy / VPC + KMS key management).
- Autoscale plan to handle weekly traffic bursts (2x baseline) and an agreed SLA for uptime and latency.
- Procurement target: sign by end of Q2, onboard in early Q3.

What Redwood recommends (high level):
- Dedicated capacity offering: reserved GPU pool (we typically size starting at 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for workloads like yours, can scale to 8+ with bursting).
- Isolation: customer VPC private deployment + dedicated tenancy and KMS integration for encryption at rest.
- Scaling plan: baseline capacity for steady throughput + burst nodes that can spin up within 60s for 2x traffic; automatic KV-cache warming to reduce cold-start impact.
- SLA targets: 99.9% platform uptime SLA, p95 token latency objective configurable per model lane (we can commit to p95 < 120ms on the configured model variant once sizing is validated).

Attached: draft dedicated-capacity proposal and a short SLA draft for your legal/procurement team to review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to share formal sizing & pricing proposal (attached) — action: Rafael will own pricing and sizing.
2) Technical deep-dive session with Dan and Michael to validate performance profile and network requirements — action: Michael to schedule (30–45m).
3) Procurement review + DocuSign flow for reserved capacity contract — action: Sofia to loop in procurement contact; Redwood to share DocuSign link once legal is aligned.

Timing: Rafael will turn around a scoped proposal by EOD Wednesday (2027-03-17). Michael will reach out to Dan to propose times for a technical deep-dive this week.

If any item above is incorrect or missing please flag and I’ll update.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dedicated-capacity-proposal.pdf (proposal, 6 pages), SLA-draft-Redwood-v1.docx (SLA draft)

From: Sofia Ramirez <sramirez@caduceus.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Li <dan.li@caduceus.health>, procurement@caduceus.health, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discussion with Caduceus Health / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this matches our notes and is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 < 120ms target looks right for the latency-sensitive endpoints (we can be looser for longer batch jobs).
- Isolation: we need confirmation that Redwood will provide separate KV cache instances and network isolation for PHI lanes; KMS integration is required (we use AWS KMS).
- Autoscale: 60s spin-up window is acceptable as long as cache warming strategies are included.
- Procurement: our timeline is aggressive — we’re aiming to complete vendor selection by 30 Jun. Pricing bands will be determinative.

Actions from our side:
- Dan will take the performance validation items and coordinate with Michael for the deep-dive.
- I’ve looped in procurement on this thread (procurement@caduceus.health) — they’ll follow up on PO and contract terms.

Please confirm when Rafael publishes the scoped pricing and any optional add-ons (long-term retention, extended observability retention). Also confirm if there are minimum term commitments required for the reserved pool.

Best,
Sofia Ramirez
Head of ML Ops, Caduceus Health

Quick internal note — Rafael here with proposed starting scope before I finalize the formal proposal: 

Sizing recommendation (starter):
- 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes configured across 2-3 model lanes (low-latency lane for 512-token p95 objectives, and 1–2 batch lanes for high-throughput jobs).
- KV-cache per-tenant and separate cache instances for PHI lane to satisfy isolation.
- Network: we’ll require VPC peering + customer-managed subnets for the private deployment; Michael to confirm exact CIDR/egress rules with Dan.

SLA / economics (high level):
- Platform uptime SLA: 99.9% (standard for Dedicated SKU).
- Latency SLO: commit to p95 < 120ms on the low-latency lane after tuning/validation.
- Pricing: committed monthly capacity pricing with burst credits; preliminary band: $Xk/month for 4-node reserved pool, plus overage/burst pricing. I’ll replace $Xk with concrete numbers in the formal proposal.

Next internal actions:
- Rafael to publish formal pricing + scope by EOD Wednesday (2027-03-17) and upload to HubSpot deal (RDW-2027-045).
- Michael to schedule technical deep-dive with Dan this week (30–45m).
- Marissa to share this thread with procurement contact if needed.

I’ll attach the proposal and SLA draft in the external send once the numbers are finalized.

-Rafael
